scope: M450 fixed-160-byte exact PWP plus correction atomic co-pack screen for the four frozen H67 ep35 bottleneck Conv3x3 operators; no new RTL, executable fragment schedule, catalog change, port change, system speedup, resource-normalized speedup, PPA, power, energy, or DATE-headline claim
verified: Executed the M430, M442, M449, and M450 seal self-checks from each corresponding result-directory cwd; every check returned zero mismatch.
Independently enumerated 442,368 frozen signed weight/correction vector cases and reproduced the exact signed-width histogram: 6 bits=6, 7 bits=70,724, 8 bits=371,638.
Recomputed exact vector payload bounds of 72 to 96 bytes.  No complete vector fits either the 16-byte wide slack or the 64-byte narrow slack, hence there are zero atomic fixed160 co-pack candidates.
Read the frozen M430 per-phase CSV exactly once and reproduced all 17,280 phase aggregates and 517,041,352 fixed160 cycles with zero upstream mismatch.
Confirmed fixed160 atomic co-pack leaves cycles unchanged at 517,041,352, exactly 1.000000x versus M430.
Recomputed the non-executable 96-byte global-fragment ceiling as 486,694,570 cycles or 1.062352826x, and the deliberately impossible all-minimum-72-byte ceiling as 476,578,975 cycles or 1.084901725x.
Confirmed even the impossible 72-byte ceiling is below the pre-frozen 1.10x continuation threshold, so further fixed160 co-pack RTL is correctly stopped.
Confirmed the M450 contract declares no raw M40 input; static AST inspection found no raw packed/value-payload path literal in the analyzer; the independent auditor itself made zero raw M40 reads.
Confirmed the M430 catalog hash and docs/359 hash were unchanged before and after review.

findings.title: Zero historical raw reads cannot be reconstructed solely from sealed outputs
findings.detail: The frozen contract has no raw M40 input, the analyzer's reachable input path is the sealed phase CSV and weight binaries, static AST inspection found no raw payload path literal, and this independent run made zero raw reads.  That is strong reproducibility evidence, but final files cannot prove the I/O history of an already-finished historical process.  Keep the qualified wording used by M454 rather than claiming forensic certainty.

findings.title: The 72-byte and 96-byte global-fragment points are ceilings only
findings.detail: They pool unused bytes across descriptors and phases without an executable catalog, buffering policy, port protocol, or scheduler.  The 72-byte point additionally forces every vector to the observed minimum even though only six of 442,368 cases have the narrowest signed width.  Both are useful falsification bounds but must remain outside executable performance tables.

claim_language.allowed: Under the frozen fixed160 interface, no complete exact correction vector fits available descriptor slack; the executable cycle count is unchanged.  Even two explicitly non-executable packing ceilings remain below 1.10x.
